about: Numbers the SNAP program (src/core2/modules/assistance.ts) uses, each tagged SOURCED (with its citation), ESTIMATED (with its source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it is checked against). Maximum allotments are not here: they are the starting law's snap-maximum rows.

earnedIncomeDeductionShare.source: 7 U.S.C. 2014(e)(2): a 20 percent deduction from earned income.

benefitReductionShare.source: 7 U.S.C. 2017(a): the allotment is the maximum less 30 percent of the household's net income.

standardDeductionSmallMinor.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP FY 2026 cost-of-living adjustments (October 1, 2025): the standard deduction for households of one to three people is $209 a month in the 48 states and D.C.

standardDeductionLargeMinor.source: USDA FNS, SNAP standard deductions by household size (FY 2026 about $223 for four people, $261 for five, $299 for six or more): the middle value stands for households of four or more.

minimumBenefitMinor.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP FY 2026 cost-of-living adjustments: the minimum benefit for one- and two-person households is $24 a month in the 48 states and D.C.

minimumBenefitMaxSize.source: 7 U.S.C. 2017(a): the minimum benefit applies to households of one or two people.

applyNeedThreshold.source: USDA FNS, Reaching Those in Need: State SNAP Participation Rates in FY 2022: 88 percent of eligible people took part nationally, and households with the least income took part at higher rates. Chosen so a household whose benefit is a tenth of the maximum is on the edge of applying; checked against the 80 to 95 percent range among eligible households.

applyLeanWeight.source: How far a person's own leaning toward filing for a public benefit (their traits, as for an unemployment claim) moves them across the line, against the size of their benefit; checked against the same 80 to 95 percent range.

participationMin.source: USDA FNS, Reaching Those in Need: State SNAP Participation Rates in FY 2022 (the low end of the range the program's take-up is checked against).

participationMax.source: USDA FNS, Reaching Those in Need: State SNAP Participation Rates in FY 2022 (the high end of the range the program's take-up is checked against).

reviewDay.source: The day of the month the monthly review of who is eligible runs, early in the month after the month's pay is in.
